question: Is a run's name set when the run is created, and visible for a run whose job never started? Can recent runs of one workflow be listed and matched by name within the request budget?
pass: Yes to both (section 6). As the story, #10, states it: (1) a run started by workflow_dispatch, whose run-name carries a unique id passed in as an input, is in the list of its workflow's runs under that name at the first read that shows it, and still under that name while its only job waits queued for a runner label no runner has, so that the job never starts; (2) one request, GET /repos/{repo}/actions/workflows/{workflow}/runs, lists the recent runs of one workflow, each with its name, and the run sought is found among them by its name alone. The cost is recorded in requests and in the rate-limit points each read uses, against the budget of section 7.3.

files.content:
# Platform trials P-17 and P-22 (combsmith/software-factory#10): is a run's name set when the run
# is created, even for a run whose job never starts, and how soon after a dispatch is the run in
# the list of the workflow's runs? The name carries the id the dispatch passes in. With runner
# "none" the job asks for a label no runner has, so it waits queued and never starts; the trial
# cancels it. It runs only when dispatched, holds no permission, and reads no secret.
name: p17-p22-run-records
run-name: sf-trial ${{ inputs.id }}

on:
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      id:
        description: The unique id this run is named for
        required: true
        type: string
      runner:
        description: hosted, or none for a job that never starts
        required: true
        type: choice
        options:
          - hosted
          - none

permissions: {}

jobs:
  trial:
    runs-on: ${{ inputs.runner == 'none' && 'sf-trial-p17-no-such-runner' || 'ubuntu-latest' }}
    timeout-minutes: 2
    steps:
      - name: Say only that the job started
        run: echo "started"
